Financial Performance

The Authority reports a surplus on the provision of services of £2.18 million for the year ended 31 March 2026 (2025: deficit of £1.24 million). This improvement is attributable to a combination of factors including tariff adjustments implemented in April 2025, a reduction in energy costs following the renegotiation of supply contracts, and lower than anticipated reactive maintenance expenditure.

Total income from continuing operations was £84.61 million (2025: £81.93 million), an increase of 3.3%. Operating expenditure, excluding depreciation and impairment, was £65.90 million (2025: £66.14 million), reflecting a marginal reduction despite inflationary pressures on materials and labour.

The Authority's net assets at 31 March 2026 stand at £312.47 million (2025: £310.29 million). The movement is analysed in the Statement of Changes in Reserves.

Capital Investment

Capital expenditure during the year totalled £28.74 million (2025: £26.91 million), of which £22.13 million related to infrastructure assets. Key projects completed during the year include:

- North Vale Reservoir dam safety improvement works (£6.82 million)
- Holmeside Water Treatment Works upgrade – Phase 2 (£4.15 million)
- Westgate trunk main replacement – sections 3 and 4 (£3.76 million)
- Stonemoor pumping station refurbishment (£1.94 million)

The Authority's capital programme for 2026-27 has been approved at £31.20 million, with a focus on continued investment in asset resilience and leakage reduction.

Borrowing and Treasury Management

At 31 March 2026, the Authority held £54.00 million in long-term borrowing (2025: £56.00 million) and £12.75 million in short-term investments (2025: £9.30 million). The Authority has operated within its prudential indicators throughout the year.

North Vale Water Authority has_fiscal_year_end 2026-03-31 date. Record status: current.

Going Concern

The Board has considered the Authority's financial forecasts for the period to 31 March 2027, including sensitivity analysis on demand, tariffs, and cost inflation. On the basis of these forecasts, the Board considers it appropriate to adopt the going concern basis in preparing these financial statements.

STATEMENT OF RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE BOARD

The Authority is required to:

- make arrangements for the proper administration of its financial affairs and to secure that one of its officers has the responsibility for the administration of those affairs, namely the Chief Finance Officer;
- manage its affairs to secure economic, efficient, and effective use of resources and safeguard its assets; and
- approve the annual financial statements.

The responsibilities of the Chief Finance Officer and of the Board in relation to the financial statements are set out below.

The Board is responsible for:

- the preparation of the annual financial statements in accordance with proper practices as set out in the CIPFA Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting in the United Kingdom;
- ensuring that the financial statements present a true and fair view of the financial position of the Authority at the reporting date and of its income and expenditure for the year then ended; and
- keeping proper accounting records that are up to date and that disclose with reasonable accuracy at any time the financial position of the Authority and enable the Board to ensure that the financial statements comply with the Code.

In preparing these financial statements, the Board is required to:

- select suitable accounting policies and then apply them consistently;
- make judgements and estimates that are reasonable and prudent;
- state whether applicable accounting standards have been followed, subject to any material departures disclosed and explained in the financial statements; and
- prepare the financial statements on the going concern basis unless it is inappropriate to presume that the Authority will continue in operation.

At 31 March 2026, the Authority had contractual capital commitments of £14.2 million (2024-25: £11.8 million) in respect of the ongoing Water Treatment Works upgrade at Bramley and the replacement of the Northgate Trunk Main. **26. Contingent Liabilities**

The Authority is party to a number of legal claims and regulatory matters arising in the ordinary course of business. The following contingent liabilities have been identified:

a) **Landfill Remediation – Old Quarry Site, Harlow.** The Authority has been advised by its legal counsel that it may be liable for the costs of remediating historical contamination at a disused landfill site formerly operated by a predecessor body. The timing of any expenditure is uncertain and dependent on the outcome of ongoing negotiations with the Environment Agency. No provision has been recognised in these financial statements as the obligation is not considered probable at the reporting date.

b) **Bond Guarantee – Regional Water Grid.** The Authority has provided a guarantee of £2.5 million in respect of a bond issued by a jointly controlled entity. The guarantee is callable only in the event of default by the entity; the likelihood of this is assessed as remote given the entity’s current financial position.

c) **Employment Tribunal Claims.** A number of employment tribunal claims have been lodged against the Authority, principally relating to equal pay and working time regulations. The aggregate potential exposure is estimated at £0.4 million, but the claims are at an early stage and the outcome is uncertain. No provision has been recognised.

The Authority has a related party relationship with its joint venture, Northgate Water Services Ltd, in which it holds a 50% interest. In April 2026, the Authority received notification from the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs of an additional capital grant allocation of £4.0 million, ring-fenced for the reduction of leakage within the network. documents.content:
Financial Performance

The Authority reports a surplus on the provision of services of £2.18 million for the year ended 31 March 2026 (2025: deficit of £1.24 million). This improvement is attributable to a combination of factors including tariff adjustments implemented in April 2025, a reduction in energy costs following the renegotiation of supply contracts, and lower than anticipated reactive maintenance expenditure.

Total income from continuing operations was £84.61 million (2025: £81.93 million), an increase of 3.3%. Operating expenditure, excluding depreciation and impairment, was £65.90 million (2025: £66.14 million), reflecting a marginal reduction despite inflationary pressures on materials and labour.

The Authority's net assets at 31 March 2026 stand at £312.47 million (2025: £310.29 million). The movement is analysed in the Statement of Changes in Reserves.

Capital Investment

Capital expenditure during the year totalled £28.74 million (2025: £26.91 million), of which £22.13 million related to infrastructure assets. Key projects completed during the year include:

- North Vale Reservoir dam safety improvement works (£6.82 million)
- Holmeside Water Treatment Works upgrade – Phase 2 (£4.15 million)
- Westgate trunk main replacement – sections 3 and 4 (£3.76 million)
- Stonemoor pumping station refurbishment (£1.94 million)

The Authority's capital programme for 2026-27 has been approved at £31.20 million, with a focus on continued investment in asset resilience and leakage reduction.

Borrowing and Treasury Management

At 31 March 2026, the Authority held £54.00 million in long-term borrowing (2025: £56.00 million) and £12.75 million in short-term investments (2025: £9.30 million). The Authority has operated within its prudential indicators throughout the year.

Going Concern

The Board has considered the Authority's financial forecasts for the period to 31 March 2027, including sensitivity analysis on demand, tariffs, and cost inflation. On the basis of these forecasts, the Board considers it appropriate to adopt the going concern basis in preparing these financial statements.

STATEMENT OF RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE BOARD

The Authority is required to:

- make arrangements for the proper administration of its financial affairs and to secure that one of its officers has the responsibility for the administration of those affairs, namely the Chief Finance Officer;
- manage its affairs to secure economic, efficient, and effective use of resources and safeguard its assets; and
- approve the annual financial statements.

The responsibilities of the Chief Finance Officer and of the Board in relation to the financial statements are set out below.

The Board is responsible for:

- the preparation of the annual financial statements in accordance with proper practices as set out in the CIPFA Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting in the United Kingdom;
- ensuring that the financial statements present a true and fair view of the financial position of the Authority at the reporting date and of its income and expenditure for the year then ended; and
- keeping proper accounting records that are up to date and that disclose with reasonable accuracy at any time the financial position of the Authority and enable the Board to ensure that the financial statements comply with the Code.

In preparing these financial statements, the Board is required to:

- select suitable accounting policies and then apply them consistently;
- make judgements and estimates that are reasonable and prudent;
- state whether applicable accounting standards have been followed, subject to any material departures disclosed and explained in the financial statements; and
- prepare the financial statements on the going concern basis unless it is inappropriate to presume that the Authority will continue in operation.

**25. Capital Commitments**

At 31 March 2026, the Authority had contractual capital commitments of £14.2 million (2024-25: £11.8 million) in respect of the ongoing Water Treatment Works upgrade at Bramley and the replacement of the Northgate Trunk Main. These commitments are expected to be incurred within the next financial year.

**26. Contingent Liabilities**

The Authority is party to a number of legal claims and regulatory matters arising in the ordinary course of business. The following contingent liabilities have been identified:

a) **Landfill Remediation – Old Quarry Site, Harlow.** The Authority has been advised by its legal counsel that it may be liable for the costs of remediating historical contamination at a disused landfill site formerly operated by a predecessor body. The estimated cost of remediation is between £1.5 million and £3.0 million. The timing of any expenditure is uncertain and dependent on the outcome of ongoing negotiations with the Environment Agency. No provision has been recognised in these financial statements as the obligation is not considered probable at the reporting date.

b) **Bond Guarantee – Regional Water Grid.** The Authority has provided a guarantee of £2.5 million in respect of a bond issued by a jointly controlled entity. The guarantee is callable only in the event of default by the entity; the likelihood of this is assessed as remote given the entity’s current financial position.

c) **Employment Tribunal Claims.** A number of employment tribunal claims have been lodged against the Authority, principally relating to equal pay and working time regulations. The aggregate potential exposure is estimated at £0.4 million, but the claims are at an early stage and the outcome is uncertain. No provision has been recognised.

**27. Related Party Transactions**

The Authority has a related party relationship with its joint venture, Northgate Water Services Ltd, in which it holds a 50% interest. During the year, the Authority purchased operational services totalling £3.8 million (2024-25: £3.5 million) from Northgate Water Services Ltd. The amount outstanding at 31 March 2026 was £0.6 million and is included within creditors. These transactions were conducted on an arm’s length basis.

Key management personnel compensation, including the Board and senior officers, totalled £1.2 million (2024-25: £1.1 million). There were no other material related party transactions to disclose.

**28. Events After the Reporting Period**

In April 2026, the Authority received notification from the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs of an additional capital grant allocation of £4.0 million, ring-fenced for the reduction of leakage within the network. This grant has not been recognised in these financial statements as it was not receivable at the reporting date.
